❣️✨A significant constitutional journey in Narendra Kumar Ram v. State of Bihar.

I am delighted to share that after successfully defending the matter before the Patna High Court, the litigation has now reached another important milestone before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

The Patna High Court held that a breath analyser report, by itself, is not conclusive proof of alcohol consumption, and criminal prosecution cannot rest solely on such a report. The Court emphasized that investigative agencies must act in accordance with the constitutional safeguards and the settled principles of criminal jurisprudence. 

The matter thereafter reached the Hon'ble Supreme Court. During the latest hearing, the Supreme Court observed that it would examine whether the police can enter private homes to conduct breath analyser tests under the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act, 2016, and further expanded the scope of the case to examine the constitutional validity of the relevant statutory provisions. This elevates the case beyond an individual dispute to one involving important questions of privacy, personal liberty, police powers, and constitutional governance. 

This litigation is not merely about prohibition law—it is about ensuring that constitutional guarantees under Articles 14 and 21 are not diluted in the name of enforcement. The balance between the State's power to enforce the law and the citizen's fundamental rights lies at the heart of every constitutional democracy.

Every legal battle that contributes to the evolution of constitutional jurisprudence strengthens the rule of law and reaffirms that individual liberties remain protected under the Constitution.

Justice must not only be done—it must be done within the framework of the Constitution.

I highly congratulate to the team of UBI JUS IBI REMEDIUM LAW OFFICE and specially Thanks to MY SENIOR BROTHER ADVOCATE AMRIT KUMAR who wonderfully present this case💐❣️
